newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany seeks EU aid for flood-hit farmers.
newsitem.headline: Germany seeks EU aid for flood-hit farmers.

text.p: German farm minister Jochen Borchert on Monday said he was hopeful the European Union would offer rapid assistance to farmers in the flood-threatened Oderbruch region.
Borchert, who was visiting the area, told journalists he had written to the EU Commission requesting aid for farmers in the regions along the German-Polish border in Brandenburg state.
Some 5,000 hectares of farmland were flooded at the moment, state government officials said.
Emergency services were working to prevent the low-lying Oderbruch basin from flooding, with some 76,000 ha of farmland at risk.
In the district of Maerkisch-Oderland, some 80 percent of beef cattle and dairy cows and 90 percent of pigs had been moved to areas further west.
Farmers had to pay for the transport of farm inputs and animals and, with many forced to abandon harvesting, they risked losing large amounts of money this year.
Borchert said many farms in the regions had already been hit hard, and land-lease payments had been waived by the BVVG, the agency controlling former communist land.
